Subject: Latency clearance & runbook for hosted migration

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we agreed on so everything is in one place: 

Recap
- Goal: validate hosted API can meet Crescent Health's p95/p99 E2E latency targets for the existing workload before a staged migration.
- Targets: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms (end-to-end, from client request to first-byte streamed response).
- Current provider baseline (you shared): rough ballpark numbers — p95 ~220ms, p99 ~650ms (we'll need exact traces).
- Traffic shape: ~350–420 qps sustained, peak bursts to ~520 qps; peak concurrent streaming requests ~18–24.

What we (Redwood) will provide by Monday: 
1) Latency test plan (attached): traffic profiles, synthetic prompt set, measurement method, and dashboards.
2) Pre-config suggestions for hosted staging (batching window, KV cache policy, streaming concurrency cap).
3) A short-run smoke environment for a coordinated two-hour live test.

What we need from you: 
- Exact trace samples or pcap/snippets for 3 representative endpoints (attach if possible).
- Confirmation of a 2-hour test window next week (we proposed Tue Aug 2 09:00–11:00 PT).
- A point-of-contact for on-call infra during the test (name + pager or Slack).

Next steps (agreed)
- Ellen to confirm test window + share sample traces (Ellen / Eng Ops).
- Jonas & Karthik to share config suggestion doc and test plan (attached).
- Run the test, collect p95/p99, token-level cost breakdown, and an early rollback plan if we see regressions.

Attachments: latency-test-plan.xlsx, sample-prompt-set.txt

Thanks — if any of the bullets above are off, please flag and we’ll update.

Jonas Weber

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few datapoints from our side so you have accurate inputs: 
- Current measured baseline (last 7 days, internal tool): p95 = 218–225ms, p99 = 640–670ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 360 qps, 95th percentile bursts up to ~510 qps.
- Concurrency: typical sustained concurrency 12–16, peaks 20–24 (mostly streaming chat sessions).
- Payload: average prompt size ~560 tokens; ~1.8 KB request payloads.

We can commit to the proposed test window: Tue Aug 2, 09:00–11:00 PT. Eng Ops will prep trace samples and a small set of synthetic traffic generators.

A couple of clarifying questions before the run: 
1) For the streaming checks — do you need HTTP/2 streams, or will chunked-encoding (HTTP/1.1) be sufficient?
2) On rollback — what is your expected fail-fast threshold so we can coordinate traffic cutover?

I’ll attach the trace snippets in a follow-up (Eng Ops will send), and Brandon (eng-ops@crescenthealth.com) will be on the call for the test.

Ellen, Jonas —

I pulled together a concise runbook for the Aug 2 test (see summary below). Full doc is attached (hosted-config-suggestions.md). High-level: we want to make the test as close to your production traffic as possible while controlling variables we can influence.

Pre-test checklist (30–60 min before window)
- Confirm test keys and IP allowlist for the test clients.
- Warm caches: run a 10-minute prefix cache fill with representative prompts.
- Set batching window to 8ms default, with a 16ms burst allowance for peak traffic.
- Configure streaming concurrency limit to 24 (matches your peak) and set graceful queue depth at 40.

Measurement plan
- Measure E2E p95/p99 across three slices: small prompts (<300 tokens), mid (300–800), large (>800).
- Capture token-level latency and request queue time.
- Use 1s sampling for system metrics and 100ms bins for tail-latency histograms.

Fail/rollback criteria (fast-fail triggers)
- If p99 exceeds your baseline by >15% for two consecutive 5-minute windows, we’ll halt ramp and revert traffic routing.
- If error rate (5xx) > 0.5% for longer than 5 minutes, fail the test.

Post-test deliverables
- Consolidated CSV of per-request latencies + traceids (we will share p95/p99, median, and token-cost estimates).
- Short debrief call (30 min) within 4 business hours after test to discuss results and next steps.

Attachments: hosted-config-suggestions.md

Karthik
Principal Engineer — Serving Runtime
